clue.text: Kingdom whose southern neighbour could become enemy?

definitions.text: Kingdom whose southern neighbour could become enemy?

parts.words: Kingdom whose southern neighbour could become enemy?
parts.note: the country to the south of this Arabian kingdom is Yemen, whose letters can be rearranged to spell the word enemy

explanation.surface: A monarchy fears that the country on its southern border might turn hostile.
explanation.walkthrough: The neighbour is never named: you must think of Yemen and notice that its letters rearrange to ENEMY, which pins down the kingdom to its north.
explanation.definitionFit: This Arabian monarchy borders Yemen on its southern side, so it is the kingdom described.

clue.text: Decline thus to raise matter, in one form

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word reads it from bottom to top, so it is turned backwards

parts.note: gas is one of the states of matter, with solid and liquid

explanation.surface: Raising a substance in a particular state causes it to sink.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag is to sink or droop, to go down.

clue.text: Cavalryman showing us his lances are new, originally

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A horseman shows off his brand new lances.
explanation.definitionFit: An uhlan was a lancer in the Polish, German or Austrian light cavalry.

clue.text: One line inside popular bar is inherent to the architecture

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the following pair goes within the word for bar

parts.note: but means except, as does bar
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single line inside a trendy pub is part of its design.
explanation.definitionFit: Something built in forms an integral part of a structure.

clue.text: A worthy person, for example

parts.note: an admirable person whose conduct others copy, one who sets the example

explanation.definitionFit: Such a figure is someone admired and imitated, a pattern of good conduct.

clue.text: Bust succeeded all-round period of prosperity

indicators.note: the word for prosperity goes all round the letter for succeeded

parts.note: a boom is a time of economic growth
S abbreviates succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A slump followed a time of plenty in every sector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like the economic collapse after a boom, but it is the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust is a woman's chest, the breast area.

clue.text: Person with a problem recollecting name, thus

indicators.note: re-collecting means gathering the letters up again in a new order

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to remember a name and says so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollecting' looks like the problem itself (remembering), but read as re-collecting it rearranges NAME into AMNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone suffering from memory loss is a patient with a recall disorder.

clue.text: Beat music of a sort

definitions.meaning: to beat on a door is to strike it sharply, a quick knock
a style of popular music with rhythmic spoken lyrics, born in hip-hop culture

explanation.definitionFit: A rap is a sharp blow, and rap is also a genre of rhythmic spoken music.

clue.text: Encounter a misfortune under ladder

indicators.note: in a down clue, the pieces before this word sit below the word for ladder

parts.note: a ladder in tights or stockings is a run
a cross to bear is a trouble or misfortune

explanation.surface: Walking beneath a ladder brings bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: The superstition about walking under ladders misleads; a ladder is a RUN in a stocking, and 'under' puts A CROSS below it.
explanation.definitionFit: To run across someone is to meet them by chance.

clue.text: As result of foul play, Len got a score like this?

definitions.text: As result of foul play, Len got a score like this?

indicators.note: foul means fouled up or tangled, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Len is awarded points after being fouled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foul' looks like the rugby offence but tells you to rearrange PLAY and LEN GOT A; the whole clue also describes the score.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby a kick at the posts after an infringement earns three points.

clue.text: They need good drivers to keep them on course

definitions.text: They need good drivers to keep them on course

parts.words: They need good drivers to keep them on course
parts.note: reads like praise of careful motorists staying on the road, but the drivers are golf clubs and the course is a golf course

explanation.definitionFit: Players hit these small dimpled spheres off the tee with a club called a driver, hoping they stay on the fairway.

clue.text: Every other part of this material is new

definitions.text: Every other part of this material is new

parts.words: Every other part of this material is new
parts.note: a fine dress fabric whose first, third and fifth letters are each N, the usual abbreviation for new

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a riddle about the spelling: every second letter of the five, starting with the first, is N, the crossword shorthand for 'new'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a sheer lightweight fabric of silk or nylon, used for dresses and curtains.

clue.text: Verify it's criminal business

parts.note: a con, short for convict, is a criminal
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: Someone confirms that a dodgy enterprise is indeed run by crooks.
explanation.definitionFit: To verify something is to establish or affirm its truth.

clue.text: Fellow always grasping opportunity as solver of cryptic puzzles

parts.note: cod is old British dialect for a fellow or chap

indicators.note: the word for always holds the next piece within it

parts.note: e'er, a poetic contraction of ever, means always
a break is a chance or opportunity

explanation.surface: A chap who seizes every chance to crack cryptic puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: COD for fellow is old dialect ('a nice old cod'); E'ER is the poetic short form of ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cracks ciphers solves encrypted messages.

clue.text: Show Us claim to be invalid

indicators.note: something invalid is unsound, here read as broken and so rearranged

explanation.surface: An American assertion is shown to be false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be invalid' tells you to rearrange the letters of US and CLAIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical is a stage show built on songs.

clue.text: Lower classes, some in poor financial position

parts.note: D and E are the lowest grades in the British social classification of occupations
a bit means some, a small amount

explanation.surface: The poorest social groups are partly in money trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: British market research grades households A, B, C1, C2, D and E, so D and E are the lowest classes.
explanation.definitionFit: An account in debit owes money, a sign of financial weakness.

clue.text: Sorts of geese and pigeons found in Essex town

parts.note: brent geese are a small dark species
wood pigeons are a common species, so wood names a kind of pigeon

explanation.surface: Several kinds of wild birds are seen in a town in Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is a county to the east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Brentwood is a commuter town in the county of Essex.

clue.text: Crockford, for example, girl found at church office

parts.note: Di, short for Diana, is a girl's name
a rectory is the benefice or official house of a rector in the church

explanation.surface: A young woman is located at the parish office.
explanation.walkthrough: Crockford's Clerical Directory is the reference book listing the clergy of the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Crockford's is a published listing of Anglican clergy, an example of a reference book of names.

clue.text: Source of change sanctioned by the monarchy

definitions.text: Source of change sanctioned by the monarchy

parts.words: Source of change sanctioned by the monarchy
parts.note: change is coins, so the source is where coins are made, under the authority of the Crown

explanation.walkthrough: 'change' suggests reform, but it is loose coins.
explanation.definitionFit: The British coin factory makes the nation's coinage under Crown authority.

clue.text: Local intake's reflected in this projection of the corporation

definitions.text: Local intake's reflected in this projection of the corporation

parts.words: Local intake's reflected in this projection of the corporation
parts.note: the local is a British pub, its intake is drink, and corporation is old slang for a paunch, so this projection is a protruding stomach

explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' and 'corporation' sound like town council business, but the local is the pub and a corporation is a big belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A paunch built up by heavy drinking is a stomach shaped by ale consumption.

clue.text: Report on King satisfactory in royal city out East

parts.note: a report is a loud bang, as from a gun
K is the chess abbreviation for king
OK means all right or satisfactory

explanation.surface: A dispatch about a monarch being in good shape in an eastern capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangkok is the capital of Thailand, seat of the Thai king.

clue.text: Bother with duck sauce

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance, something that bothers you
in cricket a duck is a score of nothing, written as O

explanation.surface: Someone is troubled by what to serve with a duck dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts, garlic and cheese.

clue.text: Act according to custom

parts.note: per means according to, as in per instructions
form means accepted custom or etiquette, as in good form

explanation.surface: Behave as tradition dictates.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform is to act on stage or carry out a role.

clue.text: Vanished with collection of ten-cent pieces, without returning it

indicators.note: here meaning outside, so the rearranged letters wrap around what follows
a collection gathers things together in a jumble, so the pieces that follow are rearranged

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

indicators.note: returning means the word it is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone disappears with a hoard of small coins and never brings it back.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a thief with coins, but 'ten-cent' splits into two pieces; 'collection of' jumbles them into EXNCT, and 'without' sets that outside TI made by 'returning'. 'pieces' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A species that has died out completely is gone for ever, no longer existing.

clue.text: Put up with what's necessary when having a row

definitions.meaning: an old and Scots verb meaning to endure or tolerate

definitions.text: what's necessary when having a row
definitions.meaning: a peg in a boat's gunwale that holds an oar while rowing

explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests an argument, but it is rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Thole means to endure, and a thole is the pin an oar pivots on when rowing.

clue.text: Carried away Lily with car — convertible

indicators.note: a convertible can be changed in form, so the letters can be rearranged

explanation.surface: Lily is thrilled with her new soft-top car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convertible' looks like a description of the car but tells you to rearrange the letters of LILY and CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To be lyrical about something is to be enthusiastically effusive, swept up in feeling.

clue.text: Top flier going directly north

parts.note: a crow flies straight, as in the phrase as the crow flies

explanation.surface: A leading pilot heads straight up.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown is the top of the head or of a hat.

clue.text: Criticise strike

definitions.meaning: to hit or rap something sharply

explanation.definitionFit: To knock is both to run something down verbally and to hit it.

clue.text: Old learner and I go to out-dated college that restricts competition

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate in Britain
taken as written
a poly, short for polytechnic, was a British college type abolished in 1992 when they became universities

explanation.surface: An elderly student and I head off to an obsolete college that stifles rivalry.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase standing for the thing that restricts competition; 'out-dated' marks the polytechnic as a vanished institution.
explanation.definitionFit: A market dominated by a few sellers limits rivalry between firms.

clue.text: Old agreement runs out at end of 1997, say

indicators.note: the letter for runs is taken away from the end of the following word

parts.note: 1997 is an example of a year
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An archaic yes expires as a particular year closes.
explanation.definitionFit: Yea is an archaic word for yes, an assent or vote in favour.

clue.text: Use it to fish for perch

definitions.meaning: the pole with line and reel that an angler casts with
an old measure of length, five and a half yards

explanation.definitionFit: An angler fishes with a long pole of this kind, and the same word names an old unit equal to a perch.

clue.text: A patient with this has to take something

definitions.text: A patient with this has to take something

parts.words: A patient with this has to take something
parts.note: sounds like someone obliged to take medicine, but the compulsion is to take, meaning steal, things

explanation.definitionFit: This disorder is an irresistible urge to steal, so its sufferer must take things.
